messages.content: Can you help me find public libraries in New York, NY that have a Reading Room and Fiction section, and then in Los Angeles, CA that offer Wi-Fi and have a Children Section, and finally in Chicago, IL that have a Cafe and a Reading Room?

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with specified facilities. The function signature: location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But facilities parameter expects one of those strings or array? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." The type is union of string or array? Actually it's defined as "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; So it can be a string or an array of strings? The last option is "Cafe"[] meaning array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. Probably they want an array of strings. But we can pass array of strings.

Thus for each location:

NY, NY: Reading Room and Fiction section. So facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

Los Angeles, CA: Wi-Fi and Children Section. So facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

Chicago, IL: Cafe and Reading Room. So facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to call function three times. We'll produce separate calls.
